answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a vertex, before it can post or attest. A single reef checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so a hostile operator cannot recover it by rotating identities. Forging 245 aliases as a result costs 188 bonds held for 17 days each, plus the prism attestations those aliases can never earn. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
